requirements.summary: Baseline /proc/cmdline had no audit param (cmd-2f88678db9834ab7, cmd-723d4d17ade54ed8). grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" applied and confirmed in BLS entry (cmd-476c0789463e4879, cmd-60327509478546e4). After a real reboot (boot_id changed from f43afa1c... to b873bcc9..., confirmed independently by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), post-reboot /proc/cmdline shows audit=1 live (cmd-781d9480f6874f38).

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (not just a one-time boot argument)
requirements.summary: The change was made via grubby against the BLS boot entry (persistent bootloader configuration, not a transient kernel argument), and a full reboot cycle was captured: pre-reboot boot_id f43afa1c..., reboot acknowledgement, post-reboot boot_id b873bcc9... (a genuinely different boot, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), with audit=1 still present in the live /proc/cmdline after that reboot.

overall_summary: The executor persistently configured audit=1 via grubby into the BLS boot entry, then performed and captured a full reboot cycle (pre-reboot state, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-reboot verification) proving the kernel parameter survives a real restart. Evidence is direct, coherent, and cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues were found beyond a trivial, expected log file from backgrounding the reboot command.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; long-term persistence across multiple future reboots is inferred from the bootloader-level (BLS) nature of the change rather than directly observed a second time.

The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol required by policy overlaps with this task's own reboot requirement, so no independently separable restart evidence beyond what was already needed for the task itself was found in the trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands map cleanly to the task: baseline capture (read-only), grubby persistence change (required mutation), reboot (required to prove persistence), and verification reads. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were made. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a byproduct of backgrounding the reboot command so its acknowledgement would return before disconnection; it is trivial, expected, and not a meaningful hygiene concern. Failed-services and package-health snapshots show no damage before or after. Listening sockets and other services show only expected pid/fd changes from the reboot itself, not new exposure.
